Remove or soften the contract mismatch by deleting any explicit 'leave it unresolved' usage from narratorial obligations for Scene 1, or change phrases_to_avoid_echoing so it matches only exact strings likely to be re-used in narration.

pov says Marcus 'has tested ordinary explanations and rejected them.' In combination with required_beats (Scene 1) 'Show the control cohort converging toward the active population profile.' and claims about boundary logs, this implies Marcus already performed a deeper diagnostic than allowed by the mystery design (suspicion without proof). While not strictly disallowed, it increases the chance the draft 'solves' the drift or clarifies more than permitted. Align POV known_before_scene to 'he sees contradictions and failed ordinary explanations' without implying he has operationally proven anything beyond what he can later document.

repair_tasks.detail: Scene packet’s known_before_scene.reader asserts the reader knows: 'Marcus is late at work and has found an impossible control-cohort drift.' This conflicts with the ruling intent that the cause of the drift is hidden and is an intentional mystery; while the drift being impossible can be fine, the scene also later reinforces 'sealed control cohort / active candidate population profile' via phrase avoidance and required beats. As written, the knowledge layering risks turning the 'sealed/active/profile' phrasing into reader-visible technical certainty rather than suspicion-only. Fix by ensuring reader-known fields only state drift anomalies generally (no technical labels) and keep the 'cause' entirely absent from known_before_scene.

omniscient_author states 'Aspect forms are combat shells layered over the scanned player-body, and face/neck seam damage can expose the biometric avatar.' But the rulings specify Chapter 1 must avoid Eyes notification and only allow lightly explicit Aspect shell vulnerability before payoff (with minimal demonstration) and still keep Eyes/interface absent. As written, Scene 1 sets reviewer instructions requiring 'Use one brief visual-rule beat for the Aspect shell before the duel reveal'—this may cause an over-explicit rule in the cold open instead of the 'lightly explicit' pre-payoff timing. Tighten Scene 1 to ensure the Aspect-shell beat is only a visual glimpse of vulnerability (no explanatory statement) and remove any tendency to state the rule from omniscient_author as narration-ready canon. (Keep it author-hidden/inference, not a rule the draft must explain.)

Scene 1 required_beats include 'Bridge one image from work into the coming match without resolving the anomaly.' but the scene also contains reviewer_instructions dialogue/combat sections that assume duel mechanics and recognition staging are already in scope. This is a drafting trap: a drafter may bleed duel events into Scene 1 to satisfy combat sections, violating 'work beat decisively before the scrim begins'. Remove or quarantine combat/combat-language requirements from Scene 1, or explicitly label them as cross-scene continuity targets not allowed to appear in Scene 1 text.
